summary: Public transport usage has rebounded to pre‑pandemic levels, delivering a full score on the ridership component. Fuel savings remain strong despite near‑zero fuel prices, but high‑mobility sectors continue to pose congestion and emission risks.

signals.detail: Weekly fuel savings of 35.7 million litres represent 42 % of the MCO peak, showing that WFH and modal shift are still delivering substantial energy reductions even with RON95 priced at RM0.05/L.

Daily PT trips of 1.49 million match the pre‑COVID daily average (~1.43 million), earning a perfect ridership component and confirming that public transport is once again the backbone of urban mobility.

Retail & Services, Logistics and Construction retain mobility scores above 85 and WFH adoption below 15 %, exposing these sectors to congestion, higher operating costs and potential productivity losses if traffic worsens.

Public & GLC employees enjoy 60 % WFH and low mobility scores, while private professionals and high‑risk sectors have limited remote work options, highlighting an equity gap in access to flexible work arrangements.
Although PT ridership is strong, the ultra‑low fuel price (RM0.05/L) could erode incentives for a sustained shift away from private cars, risking a reversal of recent modal gains.

recommendation: Introduce a modest fuel levy to raise RON95 to at least RM0.20/L, earmarked for PT subsidies and active‑travel infrastructure. Set a target of an additional 5 % weekly fuel savings and a 10 % increase in PT ridership by end‑2027, while expanding WFH incentives for high‑mobility sectors to lower congestion risk.
